chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Sulayman ibn Rushayd, from his father, from Muawiya ibn Ammar who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'The one who recites the Quran is rich, and there is no poverty after it; and if not, then there is no riches for him.'

key_terms.غَنِيٌّ: Rich, wealthy, self-sufficient — here indicating spiritual and moral richness through connection with the Quran
key_terms.غِنًى: Riches, independence, sufficiency — the ultimate fulfillment found in the Quran
key_terms.فَقْرَ: Poverty, need — the spiritual poverty of one who is disconnected from the Quran

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the spiritual richness of reciting the Quran?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) taught his companion Muawiya ibn Ammar that reciting and engaging with the Quran bestows a profound spiritual and moral richness upon a person, such that true poverty — the poverty of the soul — cannot exist alongside it. Conversely, one who lacks this engagement lacks true wealth. This teaching was given within the early Shia scholarly community of Kufa and Medina, where the Imam regularly instructed his companions on the spiritual virtues of the Quran.
